Occurrences.Kwic: 力下禪床。上堂。云：一法若有，毗盧墮在凡夫；萬法若無，普賢失其境界。若得，有無都盡，凡聖混同。南泉不用喚如如，趙州不在明白裏。譬如洪爐猛焰，豈分釵釧缾盤？明鏡當臺，休問青黃赤白。正當恁麼時，且道有照有用、能殺能活一句作麼生道？良久，云：墻壁有耳。上堂云：學道做工夫，正如人鑿井，一日見泉源，平生用不盡。且道受用不盡一句作麼生道？一滴普霑沙界潤，十方休聽轆轤聲。上堂，云：仲春天氣喜初晴，燕語彫梁有好聲，會得玄沙當日意，便能日午打三更。卓拄杖一下，云：活鱍鱍地，非常伶利，德山覰著骨毛寒，不用南山尋鱉鼻。上堂，僧問：什麼人不被無常吞？師云：只恐他無下口處。僧云：恁麼則一念通玄箭，三尸鬼失姧也。師云：汝有一念，定被他吞了。

Occurrences.Kwic: 來現成，不假外爍也。示知白關主示知白關主從上佛祖，秪是一個指迷人；一切參學，秪是一個自求人。是故諸知識更無實法與人，秪教人憤起自求生死性命之心，一朝瞥然自悟，了無一毫得失於其間也。譬如失珠之者，日久不知珠為何狀，因問知識指示，知識曰：「此珠清淨圓照，覺明無礙，更無纖毫損缺瑕玼，你但能勤而求之，則平生如意受用不盡也。」其人不知彼之所指，但自心念口言：「此珠有如是清淨圓照；有如是光明無礙；又且毫無損缺瑕玼。」行住坐臥、語默動靜，如是想念思惟至於廢寢忘餐，勞精疲神，重增迷悶終不能獲，反以善知識誑誕，誤賺我如此參求之法絕無靈驗。遂至退墮不信，此古今參學之通病也。彼知識秪與你說個形狀，恐你妄認一切瓦礫土石、泥丸魚目以為
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB174.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Juelangsheng of Tianjie. Senses.Explanation: Use it and never exhaust it: Juzhi's one-finger line, the well dug to its spring, the emperor's doubt-spot — and Baiyu's single line rolled up twenty years for want of a hearer. Dahui Zonggao, retelling the root for his hall: the nun gone, Juzhi sighed that a man of his size was outdone by a woman, and was about to burn the hut and come down the mountain when a spirit bade him wait for a flesh-body bodhisattva; days later Tianlong came, Juzhi raised the affair, and Tianlong said — you ask, I will tell you; at 'say it and I drop my rain-hat' Tianlong held up one finger and Juzhi woke on the spot — from then on, whatever he was asked, he only raised one finger, saying: I got Tianlong's one-finger teaching, a lifetime's use never exhausted; Dahui reads Langye Jue's verse for the hall — the morning-born sparrow-hawk wheels into the sky; without the strength to lift a tripod and pull a mountain, the thousand-li black steed is not easy to ride — look at this verse and you see what it is to get the one-finger teaching; and how could this be learned? Cishou Huaishen, in the hall: working at the way is like a man digging a well — the day he strikes the spring-source, a lifetime of use — and how do you say the never-exhausted-use line? One drop moistens the whole sand-realm, and the ten directions stop hearing the windlass. Fozhao Deguang, answering the emperor on Lingyun's peach-blossom waking — Xuansha had said 'right indeed, right indeed, but I dare guarantee my old brother is not through': where is the not-doubting? Your Majesty, where do you say it is? The emperor went to weigh it, and the master said: look right in the doubting — break that open suddenly, and that is Your Majesty's own never-exhausted use; asked back, he answered: a fleck of snow on the red hearth, and the emperor nodded. Qianyan Yuanzhang, at the burial of the patron Qingweng: heaven is not without feeling — a clear day picked out of the snow-pile; blessings call blessings — do you all see the stretch of field before you? This the old man made with his own hands: alive, its use unexhausted; dead, its use unexhausted; passed to sons and grandsons, again its use unexhausted — if you can see the pattern and copy it, go home and make yourselves such a field; otherwise the mountain monk will embroider flowers on the brocade. Juelang Daosheng, instructing the hermitage keeper: from the first, the buddhas and patriarchs were only pointers for the lost, and all study only seekers after themselves; like the man who lost his pearl and no longer knew its shape — the guide says: this pearl is pure and round-reflecting, bright and unobstructed, without flaw or lack; seek it diligently and a whole life everything as you wish, its use unexhausted — and the seeker, reciting the description while walking, standing, sitting, lying, forgets sleep and food and only grows more tangled, ending by cursing the guide: the old sickness of students everywhere — the guide only showed you the shape, fearing you would take gravel and fish-eyes for the pearl. Guxue Zhenzhe, opening the furnace: open your own storehouse — not one thing; carry out your own family treasure — its use unexhausted; the buddhas of the three ages use it unexhausted, the patriarchs generation after generation use it unexhausted, all beings use it unexhausted — since it is never exhausted, why is there not one thing? Get it here and clods of earth and stone are all wrought gold; miss it, and jade halls and jasper towers run to weeds — the furnace flung wide, how do you say the line that turns the common into the holy? The ten-thousand workings at rest with nothing left over — just the time the mind is empty and passes the examination. Baiyu Jingsi, in the hall: this mountain monk once got a single line, its use unexhausted to this day; I have half a mind to bring it out, but rarely meet the man for it — rolled up and held twenty years and more — which line is it? A long pause: gold is born in the Li waters, jade comes out of the Kunlun ranges. Zuliang Chaoqi, at morning assembly after the tea harvest: the vegetables and wheat in, the seedlings planted, everyone fans himself in the cool — those who get it, the use is unexhausted; those who do not, the cool breeze is granted you all the same — only be careful — careful of what? Mind you do not catch cold.
